title: Undeciphered: the Indus script
summary: Despite many attempts, the script of the Indus cities has not been deciphered. Its inscriptions are tiny, about five signs on average, and no bilingual text is known.
why: A major Bronze Age urban civilisation left thousands of inscriptions, yet not one word can be read.
question: What language did the Indus script write, and can it be read at all?
evidence: Over 400 principal signs (estimates up to about 694), mostly on seals and short single-line texts; no named rulers attested; no known bilingual inscription.
wouldSettle: A bilingual inscription, like the Rosetta Stone, or a much longer Indus text.
